messages:
incident-bot: [PAGE] Severity P1 - Canary errors spike after rollout 2026-03-14T03:56Z. Service: /v1/generate (hosted). Symptoms: 5xx rate to canary pool increased to 18% p1m. Trigger: canary-deploy-hotflip-v12.

pagerbot: PagerDuty incident 78910 created and routed to on-call. Escalation level: L1 -> L2 in 5m if unacked.

maria: acked on pd — taking initial triage. looking now.

sanjay (SRE): joining. who pushed v12? @devon?

devon (Runtime): that was my rollout, small config change to kernel selection heuristics + kvcache flag. Canary was 10% traffic. rolling out at 03:50Z.

maria: seeing 503s (upstream 502/timeout) from canary hosts in us-west1. non-canary traffic looks normal.

incident-bot: Autoscaling events: 6 new pods started in canary pool in last 3m. CPU ok, but pod restarts: 12 evicted due to OOM.

emily (Infra): OOMs? that's odd, v12 shouldn't increase memory. pulling kube events.

devon (Runtime): pushed new quant kernels and set runtime.pool.kv_cache=true. the change could increase memory usage on long contexts.

maria: quick impact check: Support shows 3 new tickets referencing 503s and realtime metrics indicate ~1.9% of total requests failing, but concentrated to embed/generate endpoints. Customers affected: 2 enterprise tenants in us-west1.

sanjay (SRE): assign mitigation tasks: (1) pause rollout, (2) reduce canary weight to 0, (3) collect heap profiles from canary pods, (4) if OOM persists, rollback.

maria: pausing rollout in the controller now.

devon (Runtime): how do I cut weight? CLI?

emily (Infra): use the rollout CLI: `rwd rollout set-weight --name hotflip-v12 --percent 0 --env prod-canary`

devon (Runtime): running now:
```
$ rwd rollout set-weight --name hotflip-v12 --percent 0 --env prod-canary
Applying change... success
```

incident-bot: Canary weight change applied: 10% -> 0% at 03:58:40Z.

maria: traffic diverted back to stable. monitoring: canary request volume dropping, errors still present on canary pods (some are restarting).

emily (Infra): collecting kube logs and OOM kills:
```
kubectl -n prod-canary logs deploy/hotflip-v12 -c runtime | tail -n 200
OOMKilled at 03:56:22 runtime/main
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
...heap dump triggered...
```

sanjay (SRE): looks like memory regression. Need heap profiles and evicted pod traces. devon, can you disable kv_cache flag remotely for the canary nodes to confirm?

devon (Runtime): toggling kv_cache via feature flags for that service: `featurectl set runtime.kv_cache false --service embed-service --env prod-canary`

devon (Runtime): applied. will monitor for restarts.

maria: after toggling, one canary pod restarted and came back healthy. error-rate down from 18% -> 4% in last 60s.

emily (Infra): rolling a short-term patch: increase JVM heap for canary pods to reduce OOM until we have a proper fix. applying k8s patch now.

emily (Infra): patched deployment resource: `resources.limits.memory: 2Gi -> 4Gi` for canary. message: `kubectl patch deploy hotflip-v12 -n prod-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"4Gi"}}}]}}}}'`

incident-bot: Resource patch applied. Note: temporary measure.

maria: quick customer comms? ops@customers flagged two tenants. want to ping account teams.

sanjay (SRE): yes. @maria please coordinate with account team and send a concise note: cause, mitigation in progress, ETA for full rollback or fix.

maria: preparing note. draft: "We observed elevated 5xx errors for generate/embed endpoints in us-west1 after a canary deploy. We paused the rollout, reverted traffic, and applied a temporary memory increase. We're investigating root cause; will update in 30m." sending to account reps now. :email:
devon (Runtime): root cause hypothesis: kv_cache change increased memory pressure under long context usage, triggering JVM OOMs on our smaller canary instance type. We'll instrument and test locally with high-context-run to reproduce.

sanjay (SRE): next actions: devon to produce repro and a patch (either memory-safe kv_cache or fallback to previous kernel), emily to run a controlled canary test with increased memory, maria to continue customer comms and track tickets, I'll own post-incident doc + severity assign.

devon (Runtime): starting repro now. posting progress in this thread.

incident-bot: Paging timeline updated: acked at 03:57Z, escalation prevented after mitigation. Incident assigned SEV2 -> downgrade to SEV3 candidate once stable 10m.

maria: will keep monitoring for 20m. current visible impact reduced to ~0.3% failed requests.

sanjay (SRE): if error rate stays <1% for 15m we can close paging. keep heap dumps and logs retained.

emily (Infra): logs and heap dumps uploaded to /s3/redwood-incidents/3854321000/ for triage. link: https://internal-storage.redwood/s/3854321000/heap-dumps

maria: closing notes: canary paused, traffic reverted, temporary memory bump applied, feature flag toggled off. Customers notified. follow-up: RCA + remediation plan + change to rollout gating to include mem regression smoke tests.

sanjay (SRE): thanks all. :thumbsup: we'll convert this to postmortem doc tomorrow.

maria: closing incident thread in 10m if stable. :white_check_mark:
